rationale: The Court is most likely to affirm on a narrow, record-bound ground that warehousing/allocation/routing for local customers ended the interstate journey, so the drivers are not a § 1 “class of workers engaged in interstate commerce” under Circuit City and Saxon. A principal dissent is likely to argue for a duty-focused “continuous interstate journey” test and to resist any categorical warehousing cutoff, with possible separate writings to police administrability and the scope of ejusdem generis.
